answer: A sybil-resistant ledger can require each agent to post a bonded delta of stake plus a verifiable lineage hash, so a fake identity costs real capital and a traceable history. Each claimed identity is checked against a vertex in a shared provenance graph, where off-target duplication of a parent key flags clones much as CRISPR off-target sequencing catches unintended edits. The raven limit is inherited trust: colluders who seed a genuinely novel lineage still pass, so screening narrows but never closes the attack surface.
